Words in English don't always follow a regular pronunciation pattern. Some vowels are usually stressed, and some vowels are normally unstressed, like /ə/ /ʊ/ or /i/.

Unstressed syllables usually contain weak vowels. You normally never stress them in words of 2 syllables or more.

Three common unstressed vowels are /ə/ /ʊ/ or /i/.
/ə/ is the sound you hear in banana.
/ʊ/ is the sound you hear in particular.
/i/ is the sound you hear in America.

You add emphasis in a sentence by stressing important words or by adding words to support your intention. You add different words to emphasize different thing or situations.

When you decide to add emphasis, you can change the stress from the principal noun to the word you mean to emphasize. This emphatic stress adds meaning and supports the effect that you want to produce in your speech.
Example:
That was a difficult test. Standard emphasis on the main noun.
That was a difficult test. Emphasis on how difficult the test was.

Remember, when you stress a word, your intonation rises and the word is said slightly longer and louder than the other words.

images.text:
Jim: Hi there, you must be Vanessa. The service representative sent me to repair your appliance.
Vanessa: Thank goodness you're here. We absolutely need to get this fridge fixed before midday.
Jim: I can't guarantee that, but I can guarantee that it will be resolved by tonight even if it means getting a new fridge.
Vanessa: Well the service rep said in no uncertain terms it would be fixed today.

Jim: That is a case of message discrepancy. Sometimes the reps have no real clue what my job entails. You have to take what they say with a grain of salt.
Vanessa: That's where the communication breaks down. The reps make assumptions and are neither educated nor trained properly. What's your guess regarding how long this will take? It's leaking brown water at the bottom and it isn't cooling anything.
Jim: I have to check the compressor and the coils but, the worst case scenario is that we can't replace them, and that means we can have a new fridge delivered tomorrow by noon at the latest. Let's see. The coils appear to be undamaged. It seems like everything is fine except the hoses are split or cut. These will need to be replaced.
Vanessa: Great. So can we have that done by say 2 p.m. or sooner?

Jim: I can't promise anything. I'll need to return to the shop to get the hoses that work with this make. I know it's vital to your business to have a functional appliance, but unfortunately this make is obsolete and the hoses fit differently. I have to locate a supplier that carries these hoses.
Vanessa: Okay, well, thanks. Will I see you in about an hour?
Jim: In all likelihood it'll take a little longer.
